key_insight: Denoising diffusion models synthesize realistic additive-manufacturing orientation micrographs and enable property-to-structure and process-to-structure inverse mappings.
engineering_relevance: Synthetic microstructures could support computational digital twins and help accelerate metal additive-manufacturing qualification while reducing reliance on costly experiments.
method: Use denoising diffusion probabilistic models to generate microstructural orientation images.
Apply classifier-free guidance to condition generation on properties or processing information.
Demonstrate a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification application.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evidence of generated-sample fidelity, but provides no dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Micrograph fidelity alone does not establish reliable downstream mechanical predictions or generalization across additive-manufacturing conditions.
paper_title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
